function: Cascaded channel estimation as denoising of the LS estimate for IRS-aided multi-user MISO uplink, with the denoiser architecture found by neural architecture search (p. 4).
system: TDD uplink, AP with 16 antennas, 6 single-antenna users, passive reflecting IRS with 64 elements; DeepMIMO case 64 AP antennas and 64 elements, 28 GHz (pp. 3, 9, 12).
method: Differentiable neural architecture search (CENAS) with truncated back-propagation bilevel optimization, searching a CNN denoiser (convolution, separable, dilated cells); supervised on noisy LS estimates, then retrained (pp. 5-8).
data_channel: Own Monte Carlo Rician simulator (60,000 training and 20,000 test samples; path loss exponents 2.3, 2, 3.6) and DeepMIMO outdoor ray-tracing scenario O1 at 28 GHz (pp. 9, 12-13).
test_conditions: Same Rician simulator for training and testing (60,000 / 20,000 samples); sweeps over SNR, IRS elements, AP antennas, pilots; separate DeepMIMO run; no cross-scenario test stated (pp. 9, 11-13).
baselines: Non-learned LS and LMMSE; learned CDRN [16] (deep residual denoiser) on NMSE and spectral efficiency; DARTS [35] compared only for search convergence (pp. 10-13).
metrics: NMSE (dB), sum spectral efficiency with MRT precoding, search loss and number of skip connections, parameter count (pp. 10-13).
complexity: Eq. (27) test-time complexity O(3^2 M(N+1)(sum D_l + D_conv1,2 + D_decoder)) in convolution counts; 0.88e5 to 2.4e5 parameters (Table I); search time at most twice training time (pp. 8-10).
openness: none released; the public DeepMIMO dataset [37] is used for one experiment (p. 13).
q1_support: p. 13: "Fig. 10 illustrates the NMSE perfomance on the DeepMIMO dataset" (outdoor ray-tracing scenario O1, 28 GHz); the main experiments use an own Rician model (p. 9).
q2_support: p. 12: "we gain insights into how changes in channel dimensionality affect the performance of our proposed method" is a sweep over N and M; the paper never states that a model trained on one configuration is tested on another without retraining.
q3_support: p. 11: "the conventional LS method, the LMMSE method, and the DL-based method CDRN [16]" are compared in NMSE (Fig. 7(a)); CDRN [16] is an earlier learned IRS channel estimator.
q4_support: p. 8: "The computational complexity of the neural network generated by CENAS during the testing phase is expressed as" Eq. (27); Table I (p. 10) gives total parameters, 0.88e5 to 2.4e5.
q5_support: p. 13: "Fig. 10 illustrates the NMSE perfomance on the DeepMIMO dataset", a public ray-tracing dataset [37]; no link to own code or data appears in the paper.
notes: Title on p. 1 matches the DOI. Area 2: cascaded channel estimation for an IRS-aided multi-user MISO system (p. 4). The main results (Figs. 7 to 9, p. 9 setup) use an own Rician simulator; q1 and q5 are met only through the additional experiment on DeepMIMO scenario O1 (28 GHz, LOS path excluded; Table II on p. 12, text on p. 13), whose train and test split is not detailed, so the reviewer may confirm. q2 is 0: the sweeps over SNR, N, M and pilots (pp. 11-13) do not state that a trained model is reused in a new configuration, and the paper describes generating networks of varying scale (p. 1, Table I on p. 10). q3: CDRN [16] is the earlier learned baseline and LS and LMMSE the non-learned ones; DARTS [35] is compared only on search convergence (p. 10). An earlier version appeared at WCNC 2023 (p. 1).
